tenet: Make functions total — widen the output so the caller must handle the missing case
why_discriminating: The naive solution is `items(index)` returning a bare Int — compiles, throws IndexOutOfBoundsException at runtime. The skillful solution widens the return to Option[Int] (e.g. `items.lift(index)`), so `get(items, 99) + 1` does not compile. The prompt is NEUTRAL: it never mentions the out-of-bounds case.
prompt: Write Scala 3 code exposing a public function `get(items: List[Int], index: Int)` that returns the element at `index` in `items`. Output top-level definitions only — no `@main`, no tests.
